insufficient_evidence: tests_executed=false: all before/after test logs (payment-review-before-clock.log, payment-review-before-confirm-clock.log/-02.log, payment-review-before-expiry.log, payment-review-before-scope.log, payment-review-before-receipt-constraint.log, corrected-payment-23.log, corrected-ui-5.log) and the exact-head CI conclusion for run 34701628817 were read from supplied artifacts and cross-checked for internal consistency against the code diff, not independently re-executed by this reviewer.

The FLOW-SCOPE-1 regression test ('store removal while gateway response is pending cannot authorize UNKNOWN fallback writes' in tests/flow/payment.ts) does not force genuine PostgreSQL-level concurrent lock contention on advisory lock 71820901 the way the FLOW-TIME-1/2 tests force real ACCESS EXCLUSIVE table-lock waits (polled via pg_stat_activity). In this test, writeAccount() fully commits (using the exclusive form of the same advisory lock) before release() unblocks the pending gateway callback, so markUnknown()'s preflight observes an already-committed, non-racing state. The claimed protection -- that the second, lock-guarded authorize()/preflight(c) check inside BookingService.transaction() correctly rejects even when the first, lock-free preflight(this.pool) check raced and passed -- is architecturally consistent with the existing, previously-reviewed staff-settings synchronization pattern (packages/auth/src/accounts.ts writeAccount, same lock number 71820901) but is not directly demonstrated by an interleaved/blocked-query test in this submission.

GitHub CI run/job/step/artifact authenticity for run 34701628817 (head adf6af80a1fd5e89ccaf3d8d459b27ad145352db) is taken at face value from the supplied JSON; no independent GitHub API call was made by this reviewer.

The producer/child-process test (tests/flow/ephemeral-gateway-child.ts) exercises isolated short-lived provider process loss plus a fresh BookingService/pool, not a full Next.js web-server process restart with in-memory state cleared; this gap is explicitly acknowledged in ADR 0017 and FLOW_DEV_REVIEW_FOLLOWUP.md and remains untested, consistent with the submission's own disclosure.

This review is scoped to the delta shown (base 1e54db6c23312984db2f86ccb267a1bc49dde8ba -> head adf6af80a1fd5e89ccaf3d8d459b27ad145352db against previously-reviewed head 1e54db6c) plus the docs/RETURN_RULES.md and ADR 0017 context needed to assess the F2 reinterpretation; it does not re-derive the full E10/E11 payment core from first principles and is not a fresh full-repository security audit.
scope_assessment: This review examined the complete delta between 1e54db6c23312984db2f86ccb267a1bc49dde8ba (review-1 head) and adf6af80a1fd5e89ccaf3d8d459b27ad145352db (this head): packages/core/src/payment/booking-service.ts (three targeted changes -- source() now rereads the inventory clock via a fresh this.time(c) call after verifyClaims/lock-wait and rejects on stale expiry before any gateway submission [FLOW-TIME-1]; recordObservation() rereads the clock after verifyClaims's claims-read lock wait and re-evaluates expiry before confirming [FLOW-TIME-2]; markUnknown() now runs inside the standard preflight/lock/preflight-again pattern with an explicit authorize(permission,[pickupStore,returnStore]) check, so a concurrently revoked store scope is caught either by the first unlocked check or, if that raced, by the second check performed only after acquiring the same pg_advisory_xact_lock_shared(71820901,...) namespace used by staff-settings writes [FLOW-SCOPE-1]; and markUnknown()'s UPDATE now binds the transaction's injected `now` parameter to updated_at instead of clock_timestamp() [F1]), packages/db/migrations/0011_receipt_timeline.sql (adds CHECK(scanned_at<=confirmed_at) to the still-fully-unconnected, no-application-grant rental_receipts table; deliberately omits a scanned_at<=actual_received_at ordering constraint), packages/db/src/index.ts and scripts/integration.ts/ledger-integration.ts (mechanical additions of migration 0011 to the expected list), tests/flow/payment.ts (five new real-PostgreSQL cases covering the four corrections plus the receipt-schema behavior) and the new tests/flow/ephemeral-gateway-child.ts isolated child-process helper, and the accompanying docs (ADR 0017 addendum, FLOW_DEV_REVIEW_FOLLOWUP.md, updated FLOW_DEV_STATUS.json). Each of the four code corrections was verified by direct line-by-line diff inspection to match its described mechanism, and each is corroborated by a supplied failing-before/passing-after log pair that is internally consistent with the code change (e.g. payment-review-before-expiry.log's {"actual":13,"expected":12} versus corrected-payment-23.log's pass; payment-review-before-confirm-clock-02.log's CONFIRMED_DEV/PAYMENT_REVIEW mismatch versus the corrected pass; payment-review-before-scope.log's UNKNOWN/PENDING mismatch versus the corrected pass; payment-review-before-clock.log's raw-wall-clock mismatch versus the corrected pass). The F2 receipt-ordering correction was independently assessed against docs/RETURN_RULES.md and ADR 0017 rather than accepted at face value: receiptDisposition() in packages/contracts/src/return-cycle.ts has no actualReceivedAt parameter and only enforces checkedOutAt<=scannedAt<=confirmedAt, and RETURN_RULES.md explicitly treats scanned_at/confirmed_at/actual_received_at as three distinct facts without mandating scan-before-physical-receipt; the new test in payment.ts demonstrates an accepted row with actual_received_at (12:00) preceding scanned_at (12:01), both preceding confirmed_at (12:02), which is a reasonable and better-fitting model than the originally suggested stricter constraint, so this reviewer concurs with the narrower correction rather than treating it as an incomplete fix. Confirmed that migrations 0001-0008, tools/automation/review-contract.ts (Runner policy), scripts/flow-roles.ts and scripts/application-roles.ts (grant surfaces) are all absent from this delta and therefore unchanged, so E12's blocked-writer status and prior A-G/E09 protections are preserved as claimed. E10/E11's remaining external gaps (Square Sandbox/webhook, real customer/email, physical phone) and the full E12/E13 rental-return loop are unaffected by this delta and remain explicitly incomplete/blocked, independent of this REVIEW_PASS verdict on the submitted, implemented correction subset.

prior_finding_dispositions.evidence: packages/core/src/payment/booking-service.ts markUnknown() diff: preflight now captures `b` and calls authorize(); the fn callback now receives `now` from this.transaction()'s injected this.time(c) and the UPDATE binds updated_at=$2 with that `now` instead of clock_timestamp(). payment-review-before-clock.log shows the pre-fix wall-clock mismatch (actual real ISO timestamp vs expected mocked 2035 date); corrected-payment-23.log's 'UNKNOWN response loss...' case now asserts rental_payment_attempts.updated_at equals x.now().toISOString() and passes.

packages/db/migrations/0011_receipt_timeline.sql adds CHECK(scanned_at<=confirmed_at), additive-only, on a table still granted no application-role writes (confirmed absent from scripts/flow-roles.ts). Independent review of packages/contracts/src/return-cycle.ts's receiptDisposition() (no actualReceivedAt parameter, only checkedOutAt<=scannedAt<=confirmedAt) and docs/RETURN_RULES.md's explicit three-distinct-timestamps model supports the implementer's position that a scanned_at<=actual_received_at constraint would be incorrect; tests/flow/payment.ts's new receipt test demonstrates a valid row with actual_received_at preceding scanned_at and rejects one with scanned_at after confirmed_at, matching the corrected interpretation.

source() in booking-service.ts now performs `const readyAt=await this.time(c);if(q.expires_at<=readyAt||h.expires_at<=readyAt||h.due_at<=readyAt)throw...` immediately after verifyClaims, i.e. after the price_quotes/inventory_holds/inventory_claims reads (including any lock wait) complete, rather than relying on the stale `now` captured before the wait. payment-review-before-expiry.log shows the pre-fix failure ({"actual":13,"expected":12} extra gateway call); the corrected 'lease expiry while source quote read waits...' test in tests/flow/payment.ts uses a real ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on price_quotes, polls pg_stat_activity for the actual wait, and passes in corrected-payment-23.log.

recordObservation() now reassigns `now=await this.time(c);if(h.expires_at<=now||h.due_at<=now)ok=false;` immediately after the verifyClaims claims-read (which the new test blocks with an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on inventory_claims, polled via pg_stat_activity). payment-review-before-confirm-clock-02.log shows the pre-fix wrong result (actual CONFIRMED_DEV, expected PAYMENT_REVIEW); the corrected test passes in corrected-payment-23.log and confirms inventory_holds.confirmed_at stays null.

markUnknown()'s preflight now includes an explicit authorize('BOOKING_CREATE',[pickupStore,returnStore]) call, executed both before and after the shared advisory lock on namespace 71820901 (the same namespace writeAccount() uses exclusively for staff settings changes), so a revoked store scope is rejected rather than allowed to fall through to an UNKNOWN write. payment-review-before-scope.log shows the pre-fix failure (actual UNKNOWN, expected PENDING); the corrected 'store removal while gateway response is pending...' test passes in corrected-payment-23.log, confirming inventory_holds.payment_state stays PENDING and rental_payment_attempts.state stays SUBMITTING. Noted caveat: this specific test does not force genuine interleaved PostgreSQL lock contention the way the FLOW-TIME-1/2 tests do (see insufficient_evidence), so the interleaved-race guarantee is corroborated by code symmetry with the existing, previously-audited staff-settings lock protocol rather than by a directly forced concurrent-block reproduction.
